sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: To be prepared for war is one of the most effectual means of preserving peace.
sentences.zh: “为战争做好准备是维护和平最有效的手段之一。”

sentences.en: Those are the words of the first U.S.
in his inaugural State of the Union Address.
sentences.zh: 在国情咨文演讲中所说的话。

sentences.en: George Washington knew a thing or two about war.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿对战争颇有了解。

sentences.en: Over four decades of military service, he took part in a number of bloody battles.
sentences.zh: 在四十多年的军旅生涯中，他参加过多次血腥战役。

sentences.en: Among them was the Battle of Trenton, in which American colonists battled German soldiers
sentences.zh: 其中就包括特伦顿战役，在那场战役中，美国殖民者与受雇于英国的

sentences.en: paid to fight for the British.
The battle was depicted in the 2000 film The Crossing.
sentences.zh: 这场战役在2000年的电影《越过大河》中有所描绘。

sentences.en: In scene after scene, the Americans thrust their bayonets into the Germans.
sentences.zh: 在电影的一个个场景中，美国人将刺刀刺向德国人。

sentences.en: They kill others with cannon and musket fire.
sentences.zh: 他们用大炮和火枪杀戮敌人。

sentences.en: Their enemies repeatedly try to regroup, but are forced to flee.
sentences.zh: 敌军多次试图重整旗鼓，但最终被迫溃逃。

sentences.en: Finally, the Germans, realizing they cannot win, kneel in surrender.
sentences.zh: 最后，德国人意识到无法取胜，跪地投降。

sentences.en: These scenes, like many depictions of war, can be hard to watch.
sentences.zh: 这些场景和许多战争描写一样，让人不忍直视。

sentences.en: But they also force us to face uncomfortable questions.
sentences.zh: 但它们也迫使我们面对一些令人不安的问题。

sentences.en: Doesn't Washington's war, and countless others like it,
sentences.zh: 难道华盛顿的战争，以及无数类似的战争，

sentences.en: prove that the realists are right?
sentences.zh: 不就证明了现实主义者是对的吗？

sentences.en: That violence is the most effective means to change?
sentences.zh: 难道暴力确实是变革最有效的手段吗？

sentences.en: That power does flow from the barrel of a gun?
sentences.zh: 难道权力真的出自枪杆子吗？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the surprising truth about what actually produces radical change,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将探讨关于什么才是真正推动激进变革的惊人真相，

sentences.en: and the profound implications for individuals and nations.
sentences.zh: 以及这对个人和国家产生的深远影响。

sentences.en: Many of us watch movies depicting war,
sentences.zh: 我们许多人看过描写战争的电影，

sentences.en: or TV shows where detectives save the day by bursting in on the bad guys, guns blazing.
sentences.zh: 或者看过侦探们在枪林弹雨中冲进坏人窝点拯救世界的电视剧。

sentences.en: These sorts of stories are based on an assumption.
sentences.zh: 这类故事都基于一个假设。
使用武力可能令人不快。

sentences.en: The surest way to get what you want.
sentences.zh: 这是实现目的最稳妥的方法。

sentences.en: As war broke out in Eastern Europe this year,
sentences.zh: 随着今年东欧战争的爆发，

sentences.en: we've been reminded again of the brutal effectiveness of violence.
sentences.zh: 我们再次被提醒了暴力那残酷的有效性。

sentences.en: At Harvard University, political scientist Erica Chenoweth
sentences.zh: 在哈佛大学，政治学家埃里卡·切诺维斯

sentences.en: studies whether this common assumption is true
sentences.zh: 正在研究这一普遍假设是否正确，

sentences.en: when it comes to mass movements for change.
sentences.zh: 特别是在涉及大规模变革运动时。

sentences.en: Erica Chenoweth, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 埃里卡·切诺维斯，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Erica, I want to look at your own journey into this area of research.
sentences.zh: 埃里卡，我想了解一下你进入这一研究领域的历程。

sentences.en: When you were a kid, your mom bought you a book called Zlata's Diary.
sentences.zh: 当你还是个孩子的时候，你妈妈给你买了一本叫《萨拉热窝的罗密欧与朱丽叶》的书。

sentences.en: You were enthralled by this book.
sentences.zh: 你被这本书深深吸引了。

sentences.en: Basically, this is the story written by Zlata Filipowicz about what it was like living as a child under siege during the siege of Sarajevo.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是兹拉塔·菲利波维奇写的故事，讲述了她作为一个孩子在萨拉热窝围城期间的生活经历。

sentences.en: As a 13-year-old kid, I couldn't help but be moved by the experiences of being a kid that were not going to be available to her, her friends, and others because of the war.
sentences.zh: 作为一个13岁的孩子，我无法不被她的经历所触动，因为战争，她和她的朋友们失去了本该拥有的童年。

sentences.en: I mean, in many ways, it's like the fascination that many people have had over the years with, you know, the diary of Anne Frank.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在很多方面，这就像多年来许多人对《安妮日记》的那种着迷一样。

sentences.en: It gives you a window into what it's like to go through the experience of war.
sentences.zh: 它为你提供了一个窗口，让你了解经历战争是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Later on, I understand you became really interested in the history of World War I.
sentences.zh: 后来，我听说你对第一次世界大战的历史产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: You'd go to the public library with your family, and you loved a book about World War I Medal of Honor winners.
sentences.zh: 你会和家人一起去公共图书馆，而且你很喜欢一本关于一战荣誉勋章获得者的书。

sentences.en: What was the appeal of the book?
sentences.zh: 这本书的吸引力在哪里？

sentences.en: Well, I think I was always really fascinated with World War I.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我一直对第一次世界大战非常着迷。

sentences.en: I can't actually remember the origins of the fascination, to be honest, but from the time I can remember, I was looking at military history books,
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不记得这种迷恋的起源了，但从我有记忆起，我就一直在看军事历史书籍，

sentences.en: and one that really caught my eye was the one about Medal of Honor winners, in part because it described these situations of heroism and courage,
sentences.zh: 其中一本特别吸引我，就是关于荣誉勋章获得者的那本，部分原因是因为它描述了英雄主义和勇气的场景，

sentences.en: but also these situations of just horrific wartime conditions, trench warfare and the types of experiences that people had just serving in the war on and off the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 但也描述了战争中极其恐怖的条件，比如堑壕战，以及人们在战场内外服役时的各种经历。

sentences.en: As an undergrad, I understand you took a military science class, so it sounds like you were developing a real interest here in military history.
sentences.zh: 作为本科生，我听说你选修了军事科学课程，听起来你当时正在培养对军事历史的浓厚兴趣。

sentences.en: Yes, I was interested in potentially serving in the Army after graduating from college, and they had an ROTC program, which I didn't eventually enroll in,
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时考虑大学毕业后参军，他们有预备役军官训练团（ROTC）项目，我最终没有报名，

sentences.en: but I did take the military science course to find out whether it was a path for me.
sentences.zh: 但我确实参加了军事科学课程，想看看这是否适合我。

sentences.en: The September 11th terrorist attacks took place during Erica's senior year in college.
sentences.zh: 9·11恐怖袭击发生在埃里卡大学四年级期间。

sentences.en: They prompted Erica to go to graduate school to better understand the nature of terrorism.
sentences.zh: 这促使埃里卡去读研究生，以便更好地了解恐怖主义的本质。

sentences.en: And there was a really influential article and later book published by a scholar named Robert Pape, who's at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 当时有一篇非常有影响力的文章，后来由芝加哥大学的学者罗伯特·佩普出版了一本书。

sentences.en: And he basically argued that suicide terrorism was on the increase because it was a remarkably effective technique.
sentences.zh: 他基本上认为自杀式恐怖主义之所以在增加，是因为它是一种非常有效的手段。

sentences.en: And, you know, there was a debate about this, and another really important article and set of arguments was emerging from a fellow named Max AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时对此有争议，另一位叫马克斯·亚伯拉姆斯的人也提出了一套非常重要的论点。

sentences.en: And he was arguing that actually, looking beyond just suicide terrorism, if you look at terrorist events and you look at sort of campaigns of terrorism or terrorist groups,
sentences.zh: 他认为，实际上，如果超越自杀式恐怖主义，看看恐怖事件以及恐怖主义运动或恐怖组织，

sentences.en: and you look at how many of those groups have actually achieved what they said they wanted, it's a remarkably low number.
sentences.zh: 看看有多少组织真正实现了他们想要的目标，这个数字低得惊人。

sentences.en: And so he was saying that terrorism was not effective, and then there was this other political scientist saying that suicide terrorism in particular is very effective.
sentences.zh: 所以他说恐怖主义并不有效，而另一位政治学家则说自杀式恐怖主义尤其有效。

sentences.en: So there was sort of a vibrant debate happening in the field, and my research was really on the question of why it is that people use terrorism in democracies,
sentences.zh: 所以当时该领域存在着激烈的辩论，而我的研究重点是为什么人们会在民主国家使用恐怖主义，

sentences.en: specifically where there are so many other methods of political expression that are available.
sentences.zh: 特别是在那里有那么多其他政治表达方式可供选择的情况下。

sentences.en: So that's sort of where I was in the mid-2000s as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我在2000年代中期所处的状态。

sentences.en: Would it be fair to say that your broad belief at this point was that power indeed does flow from the barrel of a gun,
sentences.zh: 如果说你当时普遍认为权力确实出自枪杆子，

sentences.en: from your interest in military history and your knowledge of wars past and present?
sentences.zh: 这是否公平？考虑到你对军事历史的兴趣以及你对过去和现在战争的了解？

sentences.en: And I think I would qualify it somewhat just by saying that it flows from the barrel of many guns.
sentences.zh: 我想我会稍微限定一下，说它出自许多枪杆子。

sentences.en: So, you know, and I think there are a lot of people that would make a similar assumption,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为很多人会有类似的假设，

sentences.en: that when violence failed, it was more a question of capacity,
sentences.zh: 即当暴力失败时，更多是能力问题，

sentences.en: that rebel groups or terrorist groups were using, you know, were reusing violence,
sentences.zh: 叛乱组织或恐怖组织在使用暴力，

sentences.en: but didn't have really the capacity to back up their political might.
sentences.zh: 但并没有真正支撑其政治力量的能力。

sentences.en: I just want to stop for a second to note that the intuition that you had is,
sentences.zh: 我想停一下，指出你有的这种直觉，

sentences.en: I feel like an intuition that many people have in the culture, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是文化中许多人都有的直觉，对吧？

sentences.en: When we think about, you know, how, what succeeds in terms of bringing about change,
sentences.zh: 当我们思考什么在带来变革方面是成功的，

sentences.en: whether that's change on an individual level or a group level or a political level,
sentences.zh: 无论是个人层面、群体层面还是政治层面的变革，

sentences.en: We see movies and books which are all about the use of violence and war that basically achieve people's ends.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的电影和书籍都是关于使用暴力和战争，而这些基本上实现了人们的目的。

sentences.en: And in some ways, it feels like that intuition sort of flows through our lives in a way that's often not questioned.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这种直觉似乎贯穿了我们的生活，而且往往不被质疑。

sentences.en: I mean, I think from a very early time in life, at least in the United States,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为从生命早期开始，至少在美国，

sentences.en: many children are encountering, you know, war stories.
sentences.zh: 许多孩子都在接触战争故事。

sentences.en: And whether that's about the founding of the country, whether it's about the Civil War, the Vietnam War,
sentences.zh: 无论是关于国家的建立，还是关于内战、越南战争，

sentences.en: we encounter these fairly early on.
sentences.zh: 我们很早就接触到了这些。

sentences.en: And they're sort of memorialized and mythologized in ways.
sentences.zh: 它们在某种程度上被纪念和神话了。

sentences.en: And, you know, to me, I guess I grew up with a sense that war was awful but necessary sometimes,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我想我成长过程中认为战争是可怕的，但有时是必要的，

sentences.en: or it was, you know, something that was inevitable because of the nature of humanity.
sentences.zh: 或者它是不可避免的，因为人性的本质。

sentences.en: And yeah, I think you're right that as kind of a political culture, a national political culture,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为你是对的，作为一种政治文化，一种国家政治文化，

sentences.en: there's little questioning of the utility of violence.
sentences.zh: 人们对暴力的效用几乎没有质疑。

sentences.en: So in June 2006, you were, I believe, working on your dissertation and you were attending an academic workshop.
sentences.zh: 所以2006年6月，我相信你当时正在写论文，并参加了一个学术研讨会。

sentences.en: But some of what you heard at this workshop made you skeptical.
sentences.zh: 但你在研讨会上听到的一些内容让你产生了怀疑。

sentences.en: What was the workshop and what were people saying?
sentences.zh: 那是什么研讨会，人们在说什么？

sentences.en: It was a workshop that was put on by the International Center on Nonviolent Conflict,
sentences.zh: 那是由国际非暴力冲突中心举办的研讨会，

sentences.en: which is an educational foundation based in D.C.
sentences.zh: 这是一个总部设在华盛顿特区的教育基金会。

sentences.en: The thing that was really surprising about it was that the content was all totally new to me.
sentences.zh: 真正令人惊讶的是，内容对我来说完全是全新的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the basic claim, I would say, running through all of the content was that nonviolent resistance,
sentences.zh: 你知道，贯穿所有内容的基本主张是，非暴力抵抗，

sentences.en: when unarmed civilians use protests, boycotts, strikes, stay aways, other forms of non-cooperation,
sentences.zh: 当手无寸铁的平民使用抗议、抵制、罢工、静坐、其他形式的不合作时，

sentences.en: that they can actually engage in collective action in a way that's as effective or even more effective
sentences.zh: 他们实际上可以进行集体行动，其效果与使用武装叛乱一样有效，甚至更有效。

sentences.en: than when they use armed insurgency.
And the first thing that occurred to me is that when people would refer to particular cases,
sentences.zh: 我首先想到的是，当人们提到特定的案例时，

sentences.en: like the People Power Movement in the Philippines or the Solidarity Movement in Poland
sentences.zh: 比如菲律宾的人民力量运动，或波兰的团结工会运动，

sentences.en: or the Anti-Pinochet Movement in Chile, you know, my immediate response was,
sentences.zh: 或智利的反皮诺切特运动，我的第一反应是，
这些是非常有趣的案例。

sentences.en: I hadn't really thought about them in terms of, you know, nonviolent collective action winning
sentences.zh: 我并没有真正从非暴力集体行动获胜的角度去思考它们，

sentences.en: But for any example that someone brought up,
sentences.zh: 但对于别人提出的任何例子，

sentences.en: I could think of a counterexample of where an armed revolution had succeeded.
sentences.zh: 我都能想到武装革命成功的反例。

sentences.en: Erika immediately also thought about nonviolent protest movements that had failed,
sentences.zh: 埃里卡也立即想到了失败的非暴力抗议运动，

sentences.en: like the peaceful pro-democracy protests at Tiananmen Square in China in 1989.
sentences.zh: 比如1989年中国天安门广场的和平民主抗议活动。

sentences.en: As the world watches and listens in horror, the peaceful pro-democracy demonstration in China
sentences.zh: 当全世界惊恐地注视和倾听时，中国的和平民主示威

sentences.en: comes to a violent and bloody end, crushed by waves of Chinese military forces,
sentences.zh: 以暴力和血腥告终，被一波又一波的中国军队镇压，

sentences.en: hundreds of unarmed civilians hungry for freedom, mowed down in Beijing by gun-firing soldiers.
sentences.zh: 数百名渴望自由、手无寸铁的平民在北京被开枪的士兵扫射。

sentences.en: And Tiananmen Square was not the only example of a failed, nonviolent uprising that occurred to Erika.
sentences.zh: 天安门广场并不是埃里卡想到的唯一失败的非暴力起义例子。

sentences.en: Well, you know, there's certainly plenty of examples more recently.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最近当然有很多例子。

sentences.en: The one that springs to mind immediately is the Syrian revolution.
sentences.zh: 我立刻想到的是叙利亚革命。

sentences.en: But, you know, that's another example of where, you know, you have a sustained mobilization
sentences.zh: 但那是另一个例子，你有一个持续的动员，

sentences.en: that is up against a regime that effectively decided that it could roll the dice and use extreme brutality
sentences.zh: 面对一个实际上决定孤注一掷、使用极端残暴手段
并有效镇压了运动的政权。

sentences.en: And, of course, you know, even a cursory glance at history suggests numerous examples
sentences.zh: 当然，即使粗略地浏览一下历史，也会发现无数例子，

sentences.en: I mean, and starting with, you know, the American Revolution or the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从美国革命或法国革命开始。

sentences.en: I mean, start with the Haitian Revolution and the American Revolution, the French Revolution,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从海地革命、美国革命、法国革命开始，

sentences.en: the Russian Revolution, the Algerian Revolution, the Chinese Revolution.
sentences.zh: 俄国革命、阿尔及利亚革命、中国革命。

sentences.en: So we have many different examples that leap immediately to mind.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有很多不同的例子立刻浮现在脑海中。

sentences.en: You know, most people, I think, wouldn't necessarily imagine that there's really anything
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想大多数人未必会想象非暴力抵抗真的有什么东西

sentences.en: about nonviolent resistance that could make it even compete with that.
sentences.zh: 能让它与暴力革命相提并论。

sentences.en: As Erika marshalled example after example of violent revolutions that were effective
sentences.zh: 当埃里卡列举了一个又一个有效的暴力革命例子，

sentences.en: or nonviolent movements that had failed,
sentences.zh: 或者失败的非暴力运动例子时，

sentences.en: another political scientist at the conference, Maria Steffen, threw down a challenge.
sentences.zh: 会议上的另一位政治学家玛丽亚·斯蒂芬提出了挑战。

sentences.en: Examples showing violent and nonviolent movements succeeding or failing were just that.
sentences.zh: 显示暴力和非暴力运动成功或失败的例子仅仅是例子。

sentences.en: Now, it's never possible to rerun historical events.
sentences.zh: 现在，重演历史事件是不可能的。

sentences.en: You couldn't ask the question, would the French Revolution have succeeded if it had been nonviolent?
sentences.zh: 你无法问这个问题：如果法国革命是非暴力的，它会成功吗？

sentences.en: You couldn't rewind the clock of history, run the revolution differently,
sentences.zh: 你无法倒转历史的时钟，以不同的方式进行革命，

sentences.en: and see if the outcome might have turned out another way.
sentences.zh: 看看结果是否会以另一种方式出现。

sentences.en: But Maria asked Erika if there was still a way to scientifically test which approach was more effective.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽亚问埃里卡，是否还有一种方法可以科学地测试哪种方法更有效。

sentences.en: Basically, my answer to Maria was how I would do it is I would collect data for a very long time period.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我对玛丽亚的回答是我会怎么做：我会收集很长一段时间的数据。

sentences.en: I would use every country in the world as the universe of potential cases.
sentences.zh: 我会把世界上每个国家都作为潜在案例的总体。

sentences.en: And then I would look for comparable cases that were featuring primarily nonviolent resistance and violent resistance.
sentences.zh: 然后我会寻找具有可比性的案例，这些案例主要以非暴力抵抗和暴力抵抗为特征。

sentences.en: And by comparable cases, I mean cases that were seeking similar goals.
sentences.zh: 所谓可比案例，是指寻求相似目标的案例。

sentences.en: And I would apply a hard standard to that and look only at cases that were seeking radical revolutionary goals.
sentences.zh: 我会对此应用一个严格的标准，只看那些寻求激进革命目标的案例。

sentences.en: In other words, not looking at, say, civil rights campaigns or different types of reform campaigns,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，不是看民权运动或不同类型的改革运动，

sentences.en: but look at campaigns that were trying to overthrow the incumbent national government
sentences.zh: 而是看那些试图推翻现任国家政府的运动，

sentences.en: or campaigns that were trying to push for independence,
sentences.zh: 或者试图推动独立的运动，

sentences.en: either by expelling a foreign military occupation or colonial power or through secession.
